title: crater.json
description: A crater project or package: what it is, what it depends on and how it is published.

dependency.description: A dependency: scope/name with a version, for example "evaera/promise^4", "Promise:wally#evaera/promise^4" (alias Promise, from Wally), "me/lib@path:../lib" or "me/lib@git+https://host/repo.git#v1". Version forms: ^ latest, ^1.2.3 compatible, ~1.2.3 patch updates only, =1.2.3 exactly, +1.2.3 or newer.

$schema.description: Lets editors show these descriptions. crater ignores it.

name.description: Package name as scope/name, lowercase letters, digits, _ and -. In a GitHub registry the scope is your GitHub login or organization in lowercase.

authors.description: People who made the package. Shown by crater info and on the website.

description.description: One line about the package, shown in search results and on the website.

license.description: SPDX license id, for example MIT or Apache-2.0. crater licenses and crater audit warn about packages without one.

version.description: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, for example 1.0.0, with an optional -prerelease. crater bump raises it.

keywords.description: Words that help people find the package in search.

registry.description: Where dependencies come from and where crater publish sends the package. One registry or a list, tried in order.

repository.description: Source code URL, shown on the website.

can_publish.description: true lets crater publish send this package. Keep false for games and plugins that are never published.

registries.description: Short names for extra registries, used as a prefix in dependencies: { "team": "https://github.com/Studio/team-registry" } lets you write "team#studio/combat^1". crater, wally, pesde, forest and ember are built in.

import_to.description: Where this package may run in Roblox. A server package cannot go into import_client and a client package cannot go into import_server. Monorepository packages added "as the package says" go where this points.

path_to_main.description: Entry module, for example src/init.luau. Empty or a folder without init.luau makes the package a collection of modules.

icon.description: Optional picture for the registry website, a path inside the package (.png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or a plain .svg, at most 256 KB).

path_to_definition_files.description: .d.luau files added to VS Code settings on install. A file, a folder or a pattern with * and **. Empty means every .d.luau in the package.

import_client.description: Dependencies for client and shared code, installed into the client folder from crater.settings.json.

import_server.description: Dependencies for server code, installed into the server folder.

import_develop.description: Dependencies only for development (tests, tools), installed into the dev folder and never passed on to projects that use this package.

overrides.description: Force one version (or a local or git copy) of a package for the whole dependency tree, for example when two packages need different versions of Promise: ["evaera/promise^4.1.0"].

workspace.description: Folders of other crater packages in this repository (a monorepo), for example ["packages/*"]. crater install --workspace installs them all.

scripts.description: Commands for crater run, for example { "build": "rojo build -o game.rbxl" }.

tools.description: Tools pinned to this project, owner/repo@version. Added by crater tool add, installed by crater install.

block_package_scripts.description: true refuses packages that put Script or LocalScript instances into your game (they would run code by themselves). Allow the ones you trust in allow_scripts_from.

allow_scripts_from.description: Packages that may run scripts in your game even with block_package_scripts, for example ["sleitnick/cmdr"].

exclude.description: Extra glob patterns left out of the published package, on top of .gitignore and .craterignore.

allow_files.description: Script files (.sh, .bat, .ps1 and the like) to keep in the published package. crater pack leaves them out unless they are listed here. Programs can never be shipped.

monorepository-elements.description: Makes this package a monorepository, a collection of separate packages that crater add offers to pick from: a short name for each and the dependency to add, for example { "Signal": "studio/signal^1", "Promise": "studio/promise^2" }. Empty means a normal package.

interface.description: true marks this package as an interface: it describes an API (types) that other packages implement. Find implementations with crater find-interface.

realized_interfaces.description: Interfaces this package implements, as author/name. An implementation needs an entry file named init.luau or main.luau in path_to_main and cannot be a collection of modules.
